cells.tense: The direction is yours and the heart is open at the same time.
cells.ask: Tell one person the aim, not the plan — no schedule attached. Let them know it is yours while it is still unsettled. What comes back, keep as theirs.
cells.core:
You can hold a direction without gripping it, and you can stay open while you travel. That combination is rarer than either half. The route can still change, a person can still show you something, and none of it threatens where you are going. It bends nothing to hold the two together, which is why it holds.

What keeps this working is that the openness is real, not a wait for the direction to be settled. Plans change, people surprise you, the way ahead shifts, and you keep receiving that without losing the line. The aim stays; the grip stays loose. That is the balance — it wants feeding now, while it is live.
cells.sheetLine: You hold the direction and you stay open. Both are working.

cells.tense: You are leaning ahead into where this is going, further than the day has arrived.
cells.ask: Pick one plan that has no date yet and leave it undecided tonight. Write down the aim it serves, and nothing else. If it stays open, that is not failure.
cells.core:
The sticking point is not the goal, it is being already finished with everything ahead of you. You have the ending mapped before the day gets a chance to move it, and the mapping is crowding out contact. Plans get tightened, outcomes get pre-decided, and anything arriving off script feels like a problem rather than information. From in there you will not feel this as brace. You will feel it as being on top of it — and the openness is what's being spent.

Bring it back by choosing the direction while it is still in front of you. Not from the pressure to have it settled, but from having looked and picked. When the aim comes from that steadier place, you can let the route say something back.
cells.sheetLine: You settled the outcome before the day could say anything.

cells.tense: You are still standing where you left the last stretch, while the body keeps walking.
cells.ask: Pick one aim you are already moving toward. Name it out loud to someone, once, with no report and no score. Let them say something back.
cells.core:
The direction is being run in a colder way than it needs to be, because you checked out of the present to keep going. The walking goes on and you are less available to it — making the moves without taking much in. Where you stand is a step behind the day, with the direction still aimed and no one home to meet what it brings. The aim survives this, which is the hard part.

You do not have to get the feelings back first. Get your attention back in the room you are actually in, and the rest comes with it. The aim you are running can stand next to someone hearing it, and it will not be spoiled by that.
cells.sheetLine: The aim kept moving. You stopped showing up to it.

cells.tense: You are picking up what matters before you know that you are the one picking.
cells.ask: Next time an aim catches before you can explain why, say it to the person beside you as a hunch. Not decided, not defended. Let them hear it while it is still rough.
cells.core:
You already recognize the right direction early — a pull toward the thing that matters shows up before you have the case for it. You act on it, and then you call it what the moment required, or the obvious move. The recognition is doing the steering, and this one habit keeps it unnamed. Whoever is at the table sees it land with a confidence you did not claim.

This is not a flaw in knowing, it is a habit of not signing it. Start smaller than the whole pattern: one pull, said plainly. The aim came from you before you argued with it, and saying so costs nothing.
cells.sheetLine: You name the pull after the fact. Name it while it is moving.
